title: Problem solving: number sentences
summary: Turn a story into a number sentence. Put a box □ where the number you don't know goes, then find it.
guide: This studio practises one {{term:problem-solving-strategy}}: write the problem as a number sentence, with a box □ for the missing number (□ + 4 = 9). It matches missing-number problems from Year 1 onwards and the Iranian Year 2–3 lesson on using symbols.

In each mission your child first picks the facts they need and the question. Then they place numbers in the gaps of the number sentence, tap the circle in the middle to change the sign (+ − × ÷) and put the box □ where the unknown number goes. Number sentences always read left to right.

The box can be anywhere: 27 + □ = 53, □ × 6 = 24 or □ ÷ 4 = 7. A common mistake is to guess the operation from one word ("shared", "gave"). Writing the sentence shows where the unknown number really is.

The last mission has two operations (multiply, then add), like the notebook-and-rubber problem in the Iranian Year 2 book. The "why" question at the end of each mission is the look-back step: put your answer in the box and see whether the sentence is true.

engine.step-solve: Write a number sentence and answer
engine.label-known: What do we know? Tap the facts you need.
engine.instruction-symbolic: Tap a number, then its place in the sentence. Put □ where the unknown number goes.
engine.ask-more: How many more stickers does Zahra need?
engine.ask-all: How many stickers does Zahra have now?
engine.fact-each-6: She puts 6 cakes on each plate.
engine.ask-plates: How many plates does Maryam need?
engine.ask-per-plate: How many cakes are on each plate?
engine.fact-children-4: Hassan shared the walnuts equally between 4 children.
engine.ask-walnuts: How many walnuts did Hassan have?
engine.ask-each: How many walnuts did each child get?
engine.fact-notebooks-2: Ali bought 2 notebooks and a rubber.

engine.ask-notebooks: How many notebooks did Ali buy?

missing-addend.title: How many more?
missing-addend.prompt: Zahra has 27 stickers. She wants to have 53 stickers. How many more stickers does Zahra need? Write a number sentence for it.
missing-addend.hint: 27 stickers and some more make 53. We don't know "some more", so put □ there: 27 + □ = 53
missing-addend.success: Well done! 27 + 26 = 53. Zahra needs 26 more stickers.
missing-addend.why: Why can't 80 be the answer? Put your answer in the box and read the sentence.
missing-addend.model: 53 is all the stickers Zahra wants. If she got 80 more, she would have more than 53. I put the answer in the box: 27 + 26 = 53, so the sentence is true.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap both numbers in the problem.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that: Zahra has 27 stickers. What don't we know?
feedback.sentence-empty: Fill every gap in the sentence. Tap a number, then its place.
feedback.sentence-box: Show the number we don't know with a box □. You need exactly one box.
feedback.sentence-numbers: The numbers in the problem, 27 and 53, must be in the sentence.
feedback.sentence-false: Read your sentence aloud. Do 27 and another number make 53? 53 is all the stickers, so it goes after the = sign.
feedback.added: 27 + 53 = 80 is even more than 53! Zahra only wants 53 stickers.
feedback.too-big: Put your answer in the box: 27 + your answer is more than 53.
feedback.too-small: Put your answer in the box: 27 + your answer doesn't reach 53.
feedback.empty: Type your answer in the gap.

how-many-plates.title: How many plates?
how-many-plates.prompt: Maryam has 24 cakes. She puts 6 cakes on each plate. How many plates does Maryam need? Write a number sentence.
how-many-plates.hint: How many sixes make 24? We don't know the number of plates: □ × 6 = 24. You can write a division too.
how-many-plates.success: Well done! 4 × 6 = 24: four sixes. Maryam needs 4 plates.
how-many-plates.why: Was your sentence a multiplication or a division? Why are both right?
how-many-plates.model: 4 plates of 6: 4 × 6 = 24. If we take the 24 cakes 6 at a time, we get 4 groups: 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Multiplication and division tell the same story from two sides.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap both numbers in the problem.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that: 6 cakes on each plate. What don't we know?
feedback.sentence-empty: Fill every gap in the sentence. Tap the circle in the middle to change the sign.
feedback.sentence-box: We don't know the number of plates. Put one box □ there.
feedback.sentence-numbers: The numbers in the problem, 24 and 6, must be in the sentence.
feedback.sentence-false: Read your sentence with its sign. The cakes go 6 on each plate: how many times is 6 repeated? Change the sign.
feedback.subtracted: 24 − 6 = 18 takes away one plate of cakes. We want the number of plates: how many sixes?
feedback.added: There aren't more cakes. How many sixes make 24?
feedback.multiplied: 24 × 6 would be 24 plates of 6! But there are only 24 cakes altogether.
feedback.too-big: Put your answer in the box: that many plates of 6 is more than 24 cakes.
feedback.too-small: Put your answer in the box: that many plates of 6 is fewer than 24 cakes.
feedback.empty: Type your answer in the gap.

shared-total.title: How many at the start?
shared-total.prompt: Hassan had some walnuts in 2 bags. He shared them equally between 4 children, and each child got 7 walnuts. How many walnuts did Hassan have?
shared-total.hint: We don't know how many walnuts there were. Shared between 4 children, each gets 7: □ ÷ 4 = 7
shared-total.why: The story said "shared", but you found the answer by multiplying. Why?
shared-total.model: Because the unknown, all the walnuts, is at the start of the sentence: □ ÷ 4 = 7. 4 children have 7 walnuts each, so altogether 4 × 7 = 28. Check: 28 ÷ 4 = 7. The 2 bags didn't matter.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. Tap the number of children and how many each got.
feedback.known-extra: Do you need the number of bags to find all the walnuts?
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that: each child got 7. What don't we know?
feedback.sentence-empty: Fill every gap in the sentence.
feedback.sentence-box: We don't know how many walnuts there were. Put one box □ there.
feedback.sentence-numbers: The numbers you need, 4 and 7, must be in the sentence. You don't need the bags.
feedback.sentence-false: Read your sentence: "all the walnuts divided by 4 makes 7". Where does the box go?
feedback.subtracted: 7 − 4 = 3 would mean Hassan had fewer walnuts than one child got! He gave each child 7.
feedback.added: 7 + 4 isn't enough: each of the 4 children got 7, not just one of them.
feedback.too-big: Put your answer in the box and divide by 4: you get more than 7.
feedback.too-small: Put your answer in the box and divide by 4: you get less than 7.
feedback.empty: Type your answer in the gap.

two-operations.title: Notebooks and a rubber
two-operations.prompt: Ali bought 2 notebooks and a rubber and paid 95p altogether. Each notebook costs 40p. Find the cost of the rubber.
two-operations.hint: The 2 notebooks and the rubber together cost 95p: 2 × 40 + □ = 95
two-operations.why: Why do you have to multiply 2 by 40 first? How can you check your answer?
two-operations.model: Because Ali bought 2 notebooks, not 1: 2 × 40 = 80p for the notebooks. The rest is the rubber: 95 − 80 = 15. Check: 40 + 40 + 15 = 95.

feedback.known-missing: You missed a fact you need. All three numbers matter.
feedback.asked-wrong: The problem already tells us that: Ali bought 2 notebooks. What don't we know?
feedback.sentence-empty: Fill every gap in the sentence: two signs and four numbers.
feedback.sentence-box: We don't know the cost of the rubber. Put one box □ there.
feedback.sentence-numbers: All three numbers, 2, 40 and 95, must be in the sentence.
feedback.sentence-false: Read your sentence: "two 40s and the rubber make 95". Work out the multiplication first.
feedback.one-notebook: 95 − 40 takes off only one notebook. Ali bought 2.
feedback.added: The rubber can't cost more than all the money! Take the notebooks away from 95.
feedback.too-big: Put your answer in the box: 80 + your answer is more than 95.
feedback.too-small: Put your answer in the box: 80 + your answer doesn't reach 95.
feedback.empty: Type your answer in the gap.
